title: Adaptive window fusion + speculative prefetch for embedding endpoint tail reduction
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: We observe high tail latency (p99) on the embeddings endpoint during short bursts and heterogeneous request sizes. Root causes identified in prior profiling: cold KV cache misses, kernel warmup overhead for uncommon sequence lengths, and rigid micro-batch windows that either wait too long or flush prematurely under bursty traffic.

Goal: Reduce p95/p99 for embeddings by combining an arrival-rate aware micro-windowing algorithm with speculative prefetch and lightweight kernel pinning to reduce kernel setup jitter while preserving p50/p95 throughput and keeping cost delta low.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end p99 for the 10% test tenants decreases by >=40% relative to baseline under production traffic replay
p95 improves by >=25% without increasing average token cost by more than 5%
No increase in error rate or OOM incidents in A/B canary (0 tolerable user-facing errors)
Feature guarded behind runtime feature flag and can be disabled per-tenant
Relevant telemetry (arrival-rate histogram, window sizes, kernel selection rates, speculative prefetch hit/miss) available in Console dashboards
design_notes: Adaptive window fusion: maintain a small sliding estimator of request inter-arrival times per tenant (EWMA with decay tuned to 2s), choose a dynamic flush timeout in [1ms, 30ms] and a max packet size (in requests) derived from recent throughput and SLO targets

Speculative prefetch: for requests with embeddings length > 128 or downstream similarity job flagged as ‘heavy’, issue an early KV warm (non-blocking) and pre-reserve a short-lived CUDA context to avoid longest tail of kernel cold-starts

Kernel pinning: route short-sequence requests to low-latency small-kernel path and larger sequences to throughput-oriented kernel; maintain a kernel success/failure score and prefer kernels with stable latency distribution

Hedging/duplicate probe: when a micro-window flush is delayed beyond threshold and request is near soft-deadline, issue a duplicate to a warm kernel instance with cheap priority; duplicates are canceled on first response
Fallbacks: when GPU memory pressure detected, disable speculative prefetch and fall back to existing batching policy
Telemetry: add per-tenant window_size, speculative_prefetch_rate, kernel_pin_ratio, duplicate_probe_rate metrics (tagged by model & region)
telemetry: New metrics emitted: embedding.window_flush_ms, embedding.adaptive_window_size, embedding.spec_prefetch.hits, embedding.spec_prefetch.misses, embedding.kernel_pin.choice
Dashboards to add: p50/p95/p99 vs. window_size bucket, spec-prefetch hit rate by tenant, kernel_pin latency CDF
Alert: p99 increase > 10% for service-level test tenants -> rollback feature flag
Tracing: add trace spans for prefetch, kernel-selection, duplicate-probe to correlate tail causes
experiments: Canary A/B: 1% of production tenants (low-risk) for 48h in region us-west-2
Scale-up test: run 10k synthetic parallel small-requests to measure flushing dynamics and worst-case p99
Replay test: run 7-day traffic replay against a canary runtime with telemetry to surface tenant-level regressions
Cost simulation: estimate token/GPU cycles delta using production sampler to ensure <5% unit-cost increase
benchmark_results: Local perf lab (synthetic burst) initial proto: p50=36ms (+2ms), p95=130ms (-28%), p99=210ms (-50%); GPU utilization +3 percentage points
Canary day-2 (1% tenants): p50=35ms, p95=135ms (-25%), p99=240ms (-43%); speculative prefetch hit=76% per heavy-tenant
Memory overhead: avg per-GPU reserved contexts increased by ~1.8% (within safety margin)
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag + unit/integration tests merged (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/3981)
Phase 1: 0.5% canary (non-critical tenants) for 24h, auto-roll back on alert
Phase 2: 5% canary with mixed tenant sizes for 72h, run replay tests and runbook verification
Phase 3: 25% with monitoring for cost/regressions, enable kernel pinning for selected models
Phase 4: full rollout if no regressions for 7 days; monitor SLOs and open postmortem if any regression
risks_mitigation: Speculative prefetch increases GPU context churn: mitigate by limiting prefetch concurrency per-GPU and backoff when memory pressure > 70%
Duplicate probes could increase costs: only enable duplicates when p99 risk detected and cap duplicate rate per tenant
Wrong window sizing could harm throughput: start conservative (shorter max window) and autotune using telemetry
Increased complexity in router: keep decision logic simple (EWMA + thresholds) and instrument heavily before enabling heuristics
next_steps: Complete integration tests for speculative prefetch (target: 2025-02-18)
Merge kernel pinning internal API and add canary config (target: 2025-02-24)
Run 48h replay and collect p99 deltas, prepare rollback runbook (target: 2025-03-04)
Decision checkpoint with PM and SRE after canary to proceed to Phase 2 (target: 2025-03-06)
